## The Work Model Decision Is a Talent Strategy Decision

The debate over remote, hybrid, and on-site work is not about productivity studies or office real estate. It is fundamentally a talent strategy decision that affects:

- Who you can hire (talent pool size)
- How much you pay (compensation geography)
- How long they stay (retention rates)
- How they perform (team dynamics)

### The Data

Talent Pool Impact:

- Full remote: Access to 100% of national (or global) talent pool
- Hybrid (3 days/week): Access to 35% of talent within commuting distance
- Full on-site: Access to 15% of talent within commuting distance

Compensation Impact:

- Remote roles in HCOL areas filled by MCOL candidates: 15-25% savings
- Hybrid roles: Location-adjusted pay with 5-10% "flexibility premium"
- On-site roles: Full market rate plus 10-15% premium for in-demand skills

Retention Impact (12-month voluntary turnover):

- Remote-optional companies: 13% average turnover
- Hybrid-mandated companies: 18% average turnover
- Full on-site mandated companies: 24% average turnover

Source: Internal TaaS analysis of 50,000 placements, 2024-2025.

### Decision Matrix

| Factor | Remote Favored | Hybrid Favored | On-Site Favored |
|---|---|---|---|
| Role type | Individual contributor, deep work | Cross-functional, creative | Physical, collaborative |
| Talent scarcity | High scarcity | Moderate scarcity | Low scarcity |
| Company stage | Established, async culture | Growth, building culture | Early-stage, culture-forming |
| Client interaction | None or digital | Periodic meetings | Frequent face-to-face |

### Implementation Recommendations

If going remote-first:

- Invest heavily in async communication infrastructure
- Create intentional in-person gatherings (quarterly offsites)
- Build timezone overlap requirements into role definitions
- Adjust compensation using a location-adjusted model

If going hybrid:

- Define "anchor days" (not flexible, designated in-office days)
- Design office space for collaboration (not individual work)
- Measure outcomes, not presence
- Offer voluntary remote days for heads-down work

If staying on-site:

- Compensate above market to offset flexibility gap
- Create compelling in-office experience (not just a desk)
- Allow exceptions for top performers
- Be transparent about the policy in job postings

- On-site candidates in specific markets
